title: Additive Animation Pose Layering System
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an additive animation pose layering system for a procedurally generated humanoid character.

SCENE SETUP:
- Dark gray background (0x1a1a2e). Perspective camera at (0, 1.5, 4) looking at origin.
- Ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.4) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) from (3, 5, 2).
- A ground plane (10x10, color 0x2a2a3a) at y=0.
- Procedurally build a humanoid skeleton using Three.js Bone/Skeleton/SkinnedMesh:
  - Hierarchy: root(hips) -> spine -> chest -> neck -> head; chest -> leftUpperArm -> leftLowerArm -> leftHand; chest -> rightUpperArm -> rightLowerArm -> rightHand; hips -> leftUpperLeg -> leftLowerLeg -> leftFoot; hips -> rightUpperLeg -> rightLowerLeg -> rightFoot.
  - Use simple box geometries skinned to bones for the body parts. The character should stand ~1.7 units tall.

ANIMATION LAYERS (all procedural, no external assets):
- BASE LAYER (Layer 0 - 'idle'): A subtle idle breathing animation. The spine bone gently rotates on X axis ±0.03 radians at 0.5 Hz. Always active.
- LAYER 1 ('wave'): An additive wave animation. The rightUpperArm rotates Z to -2.5 rad, rightLowerArm rotates Z to -0.5 rad. This is ADDITIVE on top of base.
- LAYER 2 ('lean'): An additive lean. The spine rotates on Z axis by ±0.3 radians (left/right lean). ADDITIVE on top of everything below.
- LAYER 3 ('nod'): An additive head nod. The head bone rotates X by -0.4 radians (nod down) then back. ADDITIVE.

Each layer has a weight (0.0 to 1.0) and an active/inactive toggle. Additive layers compute a delta from a reference pose (the T-pose) and ADD that delta rotation (as quaternion multiplication) to the result of all lower layers.

USER INTERACTIONS:
- Four toggle buttons in a HUD panel (top-left): 'Toggle Idle (Base)', 'Toggle Wave', 'Toggle Lean', 'Toggle Nod'. Clicking toggles that layer active/inactive.
- Four sliders (below buttons) labeled 'Idle Weight', 'Wave Weight', 'Lean Weight', 'Nod Weight', each range 0-1, step 0.01, default 1.0.
- Keyboard: Press 1/2/3/4 to toggle layers 0-3 respectively. Press R to reset all layers to default (all active, all weights 1.0). Press P to pause/resume the animation clock.
- A 'Blend Mode' dropdown with options: 'Additive' (default) and 'Override'. In Override mode, only the highest active layer applies (no additive blending).

STATE MANAGEMENT - Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame:
{
  layers: [
    { id: 0, name: 'idle', active: true/false, weight: 0.0-1.0 },
    { id: 1, name: 'wave', active: true/false, weight: 0.0-1.0 },
    { id: 2, name: 'lean', active: true/false, weight: 0.0-1.0 },
    { id: 3, name: 'nod', active: true/false, weight: 0.0-1.0 }
  ],
  blendMode: 'additive' | 'override',
  paused: true/false,
  elapsedTime: <number>,
  boneStates: {
    spine: { rx: <number>, ry: <number>, rz: <number> },
    head: { rx: <number>, ry: <number>, rz: <number> },
    rightUpperArm: { rx: <number>, ry: <number>, rz: <number> },
    rightLowerArm: { rx: <number>, ry: <number>, rz: <number> }
  },
  activeLayerCount: <number>,
  totalWeight: <number>,  // sum of (active ? weight : 0) for all layers
  frameCount: <number>,
  skeletonValid: true/false  // true if skeleton has correct bone count (15+)
}

HUD DISPLAY:
- Show current blend mode, active layer count, total weight, and paused status in a semi-transparent panel at top-right.
- Show bone rotation values for spine and head in a small debug panel at bottom-left.

IMPORTANT: The additive blending must actually combine rotations. When wave + lean + nod are all active in additive mode, the spine should show BOTH the idle breathing AND the lean rotation combined. Bone rotation values in __3D_STATE__ must reflect the FINAL composed result after all layer blending.
physics_constraints: Bone rotations must be NaN-free at all times. Additive quaternion composition must preserve unit quaternion property (length ~1.0). Layer weights clamped to [0,1]. Total weight is the arithmetic sum of active layer weights. When paused, elapsedTime must not change. In override mode, only the single highest-index active layer's pose applies.
